title: Replaying a choice word
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean alphabet and state set $S$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $N$ on $x$. Given a Boolean word $s$ and a natural number $t\le |s|$, there is a position $p\le t$ such that, if the run of $N$ from $c$ under the first $t$ bits of $s$ has not halted, then $p=t$; and after $t$ steps the replay machine for $N$, started from $c$ with a choice tape containing $s$ and its head at position zero, has the same configuration as the run of $N$ under those first $t$ bits, with the choice tape unchanged and its head at position $p$.
hypotheses_covered: A nondeterministic machine $N$ with $k$ work tapes, Boolean alphabet, and state set $S$.
caveat: The supplied statement refers to the replay machine for $N$, but its construction is not included in the supplied definitions; the description follows the stated choice-tape behavior.
